_authority: Every representation this factory may use, what it costs, what it needs, and how it behaves on a tablet. Reached from learning-needs.json. decide/GUIDE.md points here and must not restate it.
_tablet_floor: Every entry assumes the tablet contract: touch-first, no hover dependency, no precision pointing, targets >= 44 px, labels legible at arm's length on 800x1280, offline assets, works in landscape and degrades sanely in portrait. See review/knowledge/visual-floor.json for the measurable numbers.

needs: visual verification that the file shows what its filename claims
real_photograph.tablet: full-bleed on a dark slide; never framed in white
real_photograph.fails_when: the subject is inside a sealed system, or no correctly-licensed image of the right equipment exists
real_photograph.trap: a plausible photograph of the WRONG equipment is worse than no photograph - it teaches false recognition

annotated_photograph.tech: img + live HTML/SVG pin overlay positioned in IMAGE coordinates
annotated_photograph.source_level: 1-3 for the photo; annotation is authored
needs: pins in image space, never baked into the pixels
annotated_photograph.tablet: pin dots >= 44 px touch target; labels must not overlap body copy
annotated_photograph.why_live_overlay: annotation in the DOM survives any crop, aspect change or replaced photograph. Baked-in annotation invalidates the teaching the moment the image is re-cropped.

source_technical_drawing.tech: img, cited on the page it appears on
needs: figure number, section, page, and a RIGHTS state
source_technical_drawing.trap: publisher figures are frequently NOT cleared for issue. An uncleared figure can block a whole course from being issued. Escalate, never quietly use.
source_technical_drawing.prefer_instead: redraw as svg_diagram when the drawing is a relationship rather than an artefact

needs: the equipment must be the equipment the course actually uses
manufacturer_diagram.trap: never generalise one manufacturer's figures to another make

simplified_schematic.tech: authored SVG, built from a typed topology, not drawn by hand
simplified_schematic.tablet: one system per screen; label every element the learner is asked about
simplified_schematic.rule: Simplification is allowed. Misleading simplification is not. Dropping a branch is simplification; drawing a branch that does not exist, or implying a direction that is wrong, is not.

cutaway_section.tech: authored SVG, or a sourced drawing
needs: an on-screen statement that it is a drawing
cutaway_section.pairs_with: photograph the outside, illustrate the inside, and say which is which

needs: role=img and an aria-label describing the whole figure
svg_diagram.tablet: text >= 12.5 px at the rendered size; scale with viewBox, never with fixed px
svg_diagram.why_inline: inline SVG is themeable, annotatable, translatable and diffable. A PNG of a diagram is none of those.

svg_animation.gate: must answer the four questions in SKILL.md before it is built

html_process_visualisation.when_over_svg: when the states are discrete and the learner drives them, rather than a continuous drawn geometry

canvas_visualisation.use_only_when: the element count or per-frame maths genuinely defeats SVG
canvas_visualisation.cost: not inspectable, not themeable, not accessible without a parallel text description, and invisible to every static check in this factory
canvas_visualisation.note: the reference course uses canvas nowhere in its teaching visuals. Treat reaching for it as a signal to re-read the learning need.

interactive_exploration.tech: SVG or HTML with tap targets and revealed detail
interactive_exploration.tablet: two-stage tap on dense grids; every target >= 44 px; no hover-only detail
interactive_exploration.boundary: if the learner is being SCORED, it is a task screen - route to course-task-ux

flow_visualisation.tech: SVG path with a traced or dashed progression along the real route
flow_visualisation.rule: the path must follow the actual topology; a straight line between two icons is a box-and-arrow chain wearing a costume

before_after.tech: two states, same viewpoint, same scale, one control
before_after.rule: only ONE thing may differ between the two states, or the learner cannot tell which difference mattered

cause_effect_sequence.tech: stepped reveal, one caption per step
cause_effect_sequence.strongest_use: correcting a specific wrong mental model - name the misconception in a step of its own

timeline.rule: if the intervals carry meaning, the axis must be to scale; if they do not, do not draw an axis

comparison.tech: grid of variants at one viewpoint and scale, tap to enlarge
comparison.rule: hold the viewpoint and the scale constant. A comparison where the images differ in framing teaches framing.

needs: every plotted value traceable to a named source
sourced_chart.rule: mark interpolated points distinctly (the reference course prefixes them with '~') so nothing invented is presented as measured
sourced_chart.cite: axis units and the source, on the figure

generated_illustration.tech: raster image produced from a GENERATED_ASSET_REQUIRED brief
hard_limits: NEVER for safety-critical equipment a learner must recognise in real life
NEVER as a substitute for an accurate technical schematic
labels are added in HTML/SVG afterwards, never generated into the pixels
needs: a visible on-page statement that it is an illustration

teaches: any need where the exact wording IS the content
plain_text.rule: a legitimate, recordable outcome - see learning-needs.json plain_text_is_a_valid_decision

rejected_representations._note: These are not representations. They are what generic AI course material produces instead of one. Named so a review can point at the name.
rejected_representations.card_grid_of_prose: three to six boxes of sentences. Carries no relationship, no location, no order, no change. It is a paragraph with borders. course-module-ui owns the card as a COMPONENT; using cards as the answer to a teaching need is this skill's failure to name.
rejected_representations.box_and_arrow_chain: [BOX] -> [BOX] -> [BOX]. Asserts a linear sequence that real systems rarely have, and hides topology, direction, service and state. If the thing has spatial or system structure, draw the structure.
rejected_representations.decorative_icon_row: a row of glyphs standing in for concepts. An icon can label a thing the learner already knows; it cannot teach one they do not.
rejected_representations.gradient_hero: a coloured panel with a heading. Decoration presented as a screen.
rejected_representations.smartart_pyramid_or_cycle: a shape borrowed from presentation software, imposing a geometry the content does not have.
rejected_representations.stock_photograph_of_people: generic people in hard hats. Teaches nothing about the equipment or the hazard, and dates badly.
